title: Pux Pilot Master Design Intelligence Brain

principles.complementary: Colors opposite each other on the color wheel (e.g. Teal & Orange, Purple & Gold, Blue & Amber) generate maximum luminance contrast and vibrant visual energy.
principles.analogous: Colors situated adjacent to one another on the color wheel (e.g. Amber, Gold, and Orange) foster cohesive, serene, and harmonious atmospheric palettes.
principles.triadic: Three equidistant hues across the color wheel produce balanced dynamism with rich chromatic diversity (e.g. Red, Yellow, Blue).
principles.monochromatic: Variations of a single hue across lightness and saturation levels evoke sophisticated, clean, and understated elegance.
principles.splitComplementary: A base color paired with the two colors adjacent to its complement delivers nuanced contrast with less visual tension than pure complementary pairings.
principles.ruleOf603010: A time-tested palette balance: 60% dominant foundation tone, 30% supporting structural color, and 10% high-contrast accent pop.
principles.colorTemperature: Warm temperatures (3200K-4500K) create intimacy, nostalgia, and energy; cool temperatures (5500K-7500K) evoke tech, calm, clinical focus, and twilight moods.

commonMistakes.issue: Multiple highly saturated layers compete aggressively for focal dominance, causing ocular fatigue.
commonMistakes.fix: Apply the 60-30-10 rule: drop secondary layers to muted or neutral tones and let the hero layer own the saturation accent.
commonMistakes.mentorTip: In professional color grading, saturation is a scarce currency. Reserve peaks of +50% saturation strictly for your primary hero element.
commonMistakes.friendlyTip: Super vibrant colors! 🎨 To make your star subject really pop, try dialing down the background saturation just a bit.
commonMistakes.roastTip: My monitor is practically radiating gamma rays. Turn down that saturation before we need sunglasses! 🔥

commonMistakes.issue: Severe green or magenta tint creates an unnatural color cast, degrading organic skin tones and neutral white points.
commonMistakes.fix: Recenter tint to the [-10, +10] corridor and use selective temperature or saturation adjustments instead.
commonMistakes.mentorTip: Tint shifts white balance along the green-magenta chromatic axis. Keep tint within ±10 to maintain accurate color calibration.
commonMistakes.friendlyTip: Dramatic mood! ✨ If skin tones look a bit green or pink, nudging tint back toward center will make them look fresh.
commonMistakes.roastTip: Did an alien invasion happen or is your tint slider just broken? Recenter that slider! 👽

commonMistakes.issue: Extreme color temperature suppresses the natural dynamic range, clipping subtle midtone textures into a flat monotone cast.
commonMistakes.fix: Soften temperature toward neutral (-20 to +20) to allow authentic midtone and shadow separation.
commonMistakes.mentorTip: Color temperature simulates kelvin white balance. Extreme shifts clip dynamic range. Maintain moderate warmth (+15 to +25) for natural golden hour tones.
commonMistakes.friendlyTip: Bold temperature choice! ❄️🔥 Softening it just slightly will bring out rich textures in the shadows.
commonMistakes.roastTip: Are we on the surface of the sun or Antarctica? Bring that temperature slider back to Earth! 🌡️

commonMistakes.issue: Simultaneous high saturation and harsh contrast produces digital clipping and abrasive chromatic fringe.
commonMistakes.fix: Moderate contrast to +15 to +25 and smooth tonal roll-off between highlights and midtones.
commonMistakes.mentorTip: High contrast paired with high chroma compresses the tonal gamut. Reduce contrast by 20 points for smooth filmic roll-off.
commonMistakes.friendlyTip: High voltage energy! ⚡ Dialing back contrast slightly will give you that high-end cinematic polish.
commonMistakes.roastTip: Whoa there neon warrior, easy on the contrast before you slice a hole in the canvas! 🔪

principles.ruleOfThirds: Position primary subjects along the 1/3 or 2/3 horizontal and vertical grid lines to generate natural visual movement and dynamic equilibrium.
principles.goldenRatio: A proportional ratio of 1:1.618 (Phi) creates organic, harmoniously balanced layouts found throughout nature and classical art.
principles.negativeSpace: Ample breathing room around focal subjects emphasizes significance, elevates perceived luxury, and gives the viewer's eyes resting space.
principles.visualBalance: Distribute visual weight evenly using contrast, scale, and color density so the composition never feels lopsided.
principles.leadingLines: Lines, paths, and progressive tonal gradients direct the viewer's eye along an intentional trajectory toward the focal hero.
principles.figureGround: Clear luminance or chromatic separation between foreground elements and background context ensures instant visual parsing.

commonMistakes.issue: Subject is statically centered within a visually noisy background without clear depth separation.
commonMistakes.fix: Use rule-of-thirds offset cropping or apply subtle background vignetting (+20 to +35) to focus the eye.
commonMistakes.mentorTip: Center composition demands absolute symmetry or minimalist backgrounds. In busy scenes, offset the subject along the 1/3 grid.
commonMistakes.friendlyTip: To make your hero subject pop out from a busy background, try adding a gentle vignette or shifting the crop! 📸
commonMistakes.roastTip: Your subject is lost in the background noise like Waldo in a candy factory. Center focus or add some depth! 🔍

commonMistakes.issue: Too many competing text, sticker, and shape layers clutter the visual hierarchy and disorient the viewer.
commonMistakes.fix: Consolidate or hide secondary elements, ensuring the primary subject occupies at least 40% of the visual attention.
commonMistakes.mentorTip: Perfection in design is achieved not when there is nothing more to add, but when there is nothing left to take away. Simplify secondary layers.
commonMistakes.friendlyTip: You have lots of awesome ideas! 🌟 Hiding one or two decorative layers will let your best elements shine even brighter.
commonMistakes.roastTip: Your canvas looks like a sticker explosion at a craft store. Time to declutter and let your design breathe! 🧹

principles.hierarchy: Establish a 3-tier hierarchy: Headline (Display/Heavy 36-64px), Subhead (Medium 18-28px), and Caption/Detail (Regular 11-14px).
principles.fontPairing: Pair a high-character display or bold heading with a clean geometric or humanist sans-serif for crystal-clear readability.
principles.contrastLegibility: Maintain at least a 4.5:1 luminance contrast ratio (WCAG AA) between text and the underlying canvas pixels.
principles.safeMargins: Keep text at least 8-12% inward from canvas edges to prevent an uncomfortable trapped feeling and ensure mobile crop safety.

commonMistakes.issue: Text element is positioned too close to the canvas edge (<6% margin), producing visual claustrophobia.
commonMistakes.fix: Reposition text inward to maintain a minimum 10% safety margin from all canvas boundaries.
commonMistakes.mentorTip: Edge crowding violates typographic safe zones. Maintain a minimum 8-12% margin padding to preserve comfortable visual hierarchy.
commonMistakes.friendlyTip: Nice headline! ✍️ Nudging it inward from the edge gives it comfortable breathing room to stand out.
commonMistakes.roastTip: Your text is clinging to the border like it's terrified of the canvas. Give it some breathing room! 📐

commonMistakes.issue: Text lacks sufficient luminance contrast against the underlying background, causing illegibility.
commonMistakes.fix: Add a subtle text drop shadow, outline stroke, or place a semi-transparent scrim shape beneath the typography.
commonMistakes.mentorTip: Legibility requires contrast separation. Apply a subtle drop shadow (blur: 6px, opacity: 0.6) or high-contrast stroke.
commonMistakes.friendlyTip: Want that headline to pop instantly? Adding a soft shadow or outline makes it super readable on any photo! ✨
commonMistakes.roastTip: I need binoculars to read that text. Slap a shadow or outline on it before your audience squints to death! 👀

principles.dynamicRange: Rich blacks, well-defined midtones, and smooth highlight roll-off create cinematic three-dimensionality.
principles.vignetting: Gentle peripheral light falloff (15-30%) naturally draws the viewer's gaze toward the center third without looking artificial.

commonMistakes.issue: Low contrast and high brightness creates a flat, washed-out look lacking depth and tonal punch.
commonMistakes.fix: Boost contrast to +15 to +30 to anchor deep blacks and restore tonal dynamic range.
commonMistakes.mentorTip: A washed-out tonal curve reduces perceived depth. Anchor your black point by raising contrast to +20.
commonMistakes.friendlyTip: Boosting contrast just a touch will give your image rich depth and crisp detail! ⚡
commonMistakes.roastTip: Did we leave this photo out in the fog? Turn up the contrast and bring back some deep tones! 🌫️

commonMistakes.issue: Severe underexposure and high contrast crushes shadow textures into muddy, unrecoverable black pools.
commonMistakes.fix: Lift brightness by +15 and ease contrast back to +15 to +25 to reveal shadow texture.
commonMistakes.mentorTip: Crushing shadows destroys textural detail in low-key areas. Lift brightness or reduce contrast to preserve shadow gradation.
commonMistakes.friendlyTip: To bring back subtle hidden details in dark areas, try lifting brightness slightly! 💡
commonMistakes.roastTip: Half your image disappeared into a black hole. Lift the brightness before it is gone forever! 🕳️

principles.contactShadows: Ground subjects with soft contact ambient occlusion shadows matching the scene light angle.
principles.ambientHarmonization: Match color temperature, tint, and grain of inserted cutouts with the base image environment.
